bullets.title: AVGO: JPM raises FY27 AI backlog to $150B; Citi names top semi pick; earnings tonight
bullets.body: JPM analyst Harlan Sur raised AVGO's FY27 AI backlog estimate from >$120B to >$150B on exponential growth in inferencing demand from Google (6.5M TPU order), Meta MTIA, OpenAI XPU, and Anthropic; set 12-month PT at $500 based on CY27E EPS ~$20.45. Citi also names AVGO its #1 semi pick, modeling $22.2B Q2 sales, and notes AVGO signed two long-term agreements through 2031 with a major hyperscaler—FY27 AI revenues seen near $60B (~3x YoY). AVGO reports earnings tonight; 55% of investors surveyed expect shares to trade lower post-results, with concern about a MediaTek TPU v9 competition risk.

bullets.title: MRVL: Jensen calls it 'next $1T company'; +32% session; S&P 500 inclusion expected Friday
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company' on stage at Computex in Taiwan, citing networking connectivity as the key driver; MRVL shares surged ~32% to a record close of $290.79 and gained another ~12% pre-market. JPM noted a ~9 standard deviation retail buying event and a potential gamma squeeze from Friday 300/320 calls, with S&P 500 inclusion announcement possible Friday. Marvell CEO Matt Murphy also raised 2026 revenue guidance to $11.5B and outer-year target to $16.5B, with interconnect business projected to grow 70%+ in 2026. Marvell says copper interconnects are the 'last generation' viable at 200G, positioning CPO (co-packaged optics) as the future.

bullets.title: PANW: Beat-and-raise with organic acceleration; stock -3% AH on debate over inorganic mix
bullets.body: PANW delivered F3Q revenue of $3.0B (+31% YoY, beating consensus by $510M), EPS $0.85 vs $0.79 est, NGS ARR of $8.13B (+60% YoY), and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $11.415-11.425B. The beat was largely inorganic (CyberArk/Chronosphere ~$180M of ARR beat), with organic NNARR ~$370M growing ~19% YoY. Sell-side consensus is 80% Buy with average PT raised to ~$295; Berenberg raised to $360, Wedbush to $340. Stock fell ~3% AH on uncertainty over organic vs. inorganic guidance composition. Read-through: ~110 net new platformizations in Q3 (vs. ~60 in Q1), physical firewall bookings +40% YoY, SASE ARR +40% YoY.

bullets.title: SNOW: Investor Day confirms AI inflection; Piper raises PT to $320, UBS to $370, Citi maintains Buy $1,240 at EQIX
bullets.body: SNOW's user conference (20K attendees) launched its agentic CoCo platform showing 70-80% accuracy/cost improvement vs. leading LLMs; CEO targets GAAP profitability by 4Q FY28. Piper raised PT to $320 and Mizuho reiterates Outperform at $295; UBS raised PT to $370 based on 17.5x CY27E EV/S. Separately, Citi added EQIX to its Focus List with a Buy rating and $1,240 PT, citing accelerating revenue growth from AI edge/inference demand—enterprise signings have ramped from 250 kW to 1 MW, renewals generating ~25% cash-on-cash returns.

bullets.title: AAPL: WWDC June 8 expected to showcase Gemini-based Siri overhaul; JPM sees historical ~11% outperformance ahead
bullets.body: JPM maintains Overweight on AAPL; WWDC June 8 expected to debut a material Siri overhaul (standalone chatbot, multi-command, on-screen intelligence) shifting from ChatGPT-only to a Gemini-based platform. A foldable iPhone and touch-screen Mac are expected in 2H26; base models delayed to C1Q27. Historically, AAPL outperforms S&P by ~11% on average in the June-September period leading to fall launches. GS TMT also flagged AAPL as a critical AI distribution channel.

bullets.title: NVDA: Vera CPU targets $20B TAM; PC/DGX Station announcements add $300B market cap; FCF return extended
bullets.body: NVDA at Computex launched Vera CPU (80% faster than x86 on agentic tasks), RTX Spark N1X AI PC (128GB LPDDR5X, runs 120B parameter LLMs), and DGX Station with 748GB total memory. The PC announcement added ~$300B market cap; ARM gained ~$60B. NVDA also extended its 50% FCF return policy to perpetuity. Jefferies Asia semis tour notes NVDA Vera CPUs may eventually exceed GPU share. Citi maintains $300 PT on 28x C27E EPS of ~$11.9.

bullets.title: INTC: +6% pre-market on '1 CPU per 1 GPU' thesis from Computex; 18A ramping to high volume
bullets.body: INTC surged 5-6% after Computex coverage highlighted the 'one CPU per one GPU' thesis and Nikkei articles on AI-driven demand. Intel's 18A process has ramped to high volume with 14A on track; CPU demand inflecting sharply with rising ASPs. Foundry breakeven targeted by end-2027. UBS noted the stock benefited from a broader Computex AI infrastructure re-rating.

bullets.title: T: Oppenheimer downgrades to Perform on SpaceX/LEO satellite competition risk
bullets.body: OPCO downgraded AT&T (T) from Outperform to Perform citing LEO satellite competition risk to broadband and mobile from SpaceX, which OPCO now says is targeting majority broadband market share with commercial service in ~1 year. OPCO raised its 2030E US broadband subs estimate for SpaceX from 10M to 15M. OPCO prefers VZ and TMUS positioning over T; cable faces 1.5-3% annual subscriber declines. GS TMT also noted T downgraded to Perform.

bullets.title: WULF: Morgan Stanley raises PT 58% to $66.50 on Muskie acquisition; Oppenheimer also raises to $35
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised WULF PT by 58% to $66.50 following the Muskie acquisition which adds 1+ GW of Eastern Kentucky campus capacity—directly benefiting from AI datacenter power demand. Oppenheimer also raised WULF from $25 to $35. AI datacenter infrastructure renting at $20-30M per MW vs. $2M for standard facilities.

bullets.title: CSCO: Overweight maintained; Cloud Control platform launch and $100-200B refresh TAM highlighted
bullets.body: JPM maintained Overweight on CSCO post-Cisco Live; Cloud Control is now live in the US spanning networking, security, and observability with agentic security. Enterprise campus refresh TAM estimated at $100-200B with only mid-single digits of install base replaced. Agentic workflow-driven traffic inflection expected; smart switches at ~5% of purchases signal strong security-driven tailwinds. CSCO is cautious on CPO adoption, preferring NPO solutions ramping 2H27.

bullets.title: MSFT: Build keynote features 7 new AI models, Majorana 2 quantum chip, Maia 200 outperforms GB200
bullets.body: At Microsoft Build, MSFT announced 7 new AI models (MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning, coding specialization), launched Project Solara for agentic workflows, unveiled Majorana 2 quantum chip targeting 2029 commercialization, and demonstrated Maia 200 custom silicon achieving 1.4x performance/watt vs. Nvidia GB200. Azure added more data center capacity in last 18 months than its first decade. KeyBanc reiterates Overweight with $600 PT. European digital sovereignty concerns remain a longer-term risk to terminal value (France, Germany, Denmark migrations underway).

bullets.title: MU: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $1,050; WSTS forecasts 2026 semi market +90% to $1.51T with memory +250%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised MU PT to $1,050 citing AI-driven memory inflation across HBM, DRAM, enterprise SSDs with prices up 6x YoY; smartphone/PC memory faces 12-15% shortage despite 30% capacity expansion by 2027. WSTS raised 2026 semiconductor market forecast to $1.51T (+90%), with memory segment alone expected +250% to $800B+. China NAND market share now rivals Micron and SanDisk—a competitive risk worth monitoring.

bullets.title: WBD/PSKY: EU sets July 7 deadline on Paramount-Skydance/WBD acquisition at $31/share, $110B EV
bullets.body: The EU notified of the Paramount Skydance acquisition of WBD for $31.00/share ($81B equity, $110B EV at 7.5x 2026 EBITDA fully synergized) on June 2, with a provisional EU decision deadline of July 7. Transaction expected to close Q3 2026; WBD shareholders receive $0.25/share quarterly ticking fee if not closed by September 30.

bullets.title: EQIX and DLR: Both data center REITs capacity-constrained with pricing power extending to 2028
bullets.body: JPM meetings at REITweek noted EQIX enterprise demand has ramped to 500kW-1MW signings, renewals running ~25% cash-on-cash returns, and margins guided at ~51% this year. DLR has ~1.2 GW under construction, ~5 GW power bank 40-45% utilized with remainder expected under ESAs in 12-18 months; capacity largely sold out through 2027 with customers booking 2028. DLR signing 3-4% escalators on renewals. Key risks: labor and equipment supply chains.

bullets.title: ORCL: Mizuho adds as June top pick; FQ4 catalyst on IaaS revenue and $553B RPO validation
bullets.body: Mizuho added ORCL as its #1 Outperform pick for June 2026. FQ4 IaaS revenue expected at $5.7B (+90% YoY) with FY27 acceleration to 34% revenue growth. FCF inflects positive at $4B in FY29E, accelerating to $36B in FY30E. Mizuho $320 PT applies 21x EPS on FY30 estimate. $553B OCI RPO validates AI cloud demand visibility.

bullets.title: GOOGL: UK CMA imposes strategic market status designation; publishers get AI opt-out tools
bullets.body: UK CMA designated Google with strategic market status in general search, imposing conduct requirements including publisher opt-out from AI model fine-tuning and clear attribution links in AI-generated results. Separately, a Swedish court delayed the PriceRunner antitrust damages judgment ($8.3B claim) from June 10 to June 26. Publishers report lower traffic from AI Overviews.

bullets.title: META: Morgan Stanley initiates as top pick with $775 PT on search, subscriptions, and Neocloud
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley initiated META with a positive view and $775 PT (~30% upside), citing four new product catalysts (search, consumer/business subscriptions, core ad upside, Neocloud) each potentially adding $1-3 to '28 EPS. GS also highlighted META's frontier AI lab as a key beneficiary of observability platforms.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR: NVDA CPO/NVLink Fusion ecosystem positions both as primary photonics suppliers
bullets.body: Multiple X posts indicate NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion ecosystem (with Ayar Labs joining June 3) uses GFS (germanium-free substrate) where Sivers Semiconductors is the reference laser supplier, while LITE (Lumentum) and COHR (Coherent) are in NVIDIA's own photonics program. JPM is hosting an APAC investor call with Lumentum management June 5. GLW (Corning) surged 13% on Wiwynn CPO supply chain visibility. Jefferies flagged LITE down 2.6% pre-market.

bullets.title: IREN: +5.7% pre-market on 800MW data center transmission agreement in South Australia
bullets.body: IREN rose 5.7% pre-market after announcing an 800MW data center transmission agreement in South Australia, aligning with AI infrastructure/power themes highlighted across Computex.

bullets.title: WDC: Exchanges $858M of 2028 convertible notes for cash and stock
bullets.body: Western Digital entered exchange agreements on June 2 to retire approximately $858.4M of 3.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 in exchange for cash plus common stock, with the stock portion calculated using VWAP over a June 3-4 measurement period—a dilutive but balance sheet-positive transaction.
